tracking._readme: Resend domain tracking. Open and click tracking must also be enabled on the domain in the Resend dashboard, and delivery events need the webhook below pointed at this pad.
tracking._setup: all three of these must be true, or opens/clicks silently never arrive: tracking enabled on the Resend domain, a verified CNAME for the tracking subdomain (analytics -> links1.resend-dns.com for eu-west-1), and the webhook subscribed to email.opened + email.clicked. See docs/TRACKERS.md.

leads._readme: Optional CRM tab. enabled:false hides it. stages are the pipeline (terminal:true ends the progression), dueDays is the follow-up cadence in days between sends, redraftReasons are the chips offered when you send a draft back.
leads._inbox_readme: discoverFromInbox:true turns a new inbound sender into a lead (a reply is a warm lead). ignoreSenders: exact addresses or domains (and their subdomains) that must never become leads - put your tools and your own domain here.

_tabs_readme: tabs render in order; an optional "group" prints a heading before the first tab of that group (Emails holds Compose/Drafts/Sent/Received/Trackers, Insights holds Analytics). A tab without a panel is hidden automatically.

analytics._readme: Website-side analytics for the Analytics tab. Keys stay server-side. Leave a provider blank to see exactly what it needs in the UI; an MCP client can also push metrics to POST /api/analytics/ingest with the pad token.

_templates_readme: The draft architecture: email 1 shows 2-3 quick wins with what each costs, then one curiosity paragraph that out-weighs them, then the agency line. Follow-ups reveal one tier at a time (medium, then high) and always keep one thing open. Slots the pipeline fills: company, first_name, metro, service, position, quick_win_N, quick_win_N_cost, medium_finding_N, medium_finding_N_cost, medium_tease, high_finding, high_finding_cost, high_tease. Tier definitions: the seo-local and seo-geo skills.
